meta.title: Unipedia — Know what to study now
meta.description: Unipedia knows your semester: it plans your study around your tests, protects your focus, quizzes you on your own notes and shows what actually stuck. For secondary school and university.

hero.kicker: Study companion · Secondary school and university
hero.sub: Unipedia knows your courses, your tests and your notes. Open the app and one thing is waiting: the right block, with the reason why. Finish the block and you know what stuck.

promise.text: and know what to study now.

how.title: From timetable to test,
how.sub: One photo to get started, a plan that sorts itself out, your materials in one place and a Uni for every course.

start.label: Get started
start.title: One photo of your timetable and your courses appear
start.body: Take a screenshot of your timetable and Uni recognises your courses, classes and assessments. Another photo of your test dates and the semester is set up.
start.detail: Also via Google Calendar, an .ics file or text from your portal.

plan.label: Plan
plan.title: A plan that knows your tests
plan.body: Blocks spread across the week based on the dates and weight of each assessment. If a day doesn't happen, what slipped fits back in.

materials.label: Materials
materials.title: Your PDFs, Drives and folders in one place
materials.body: Connect Google Drive, your course's shared folders or folders on your computer. The app sorts everything by course and Uni uses it to answer.
materials.detail: Past papers, course notes, slides and worksheets, by course.

measure.label: Progress
measure.title: See what stuck, not just the time
measure.body: Estimated retention per course, reviews due, consistency and each Uni's real mastery. Estimates are shown as estimates.
measure.detail: Up to 3 priorities a week, not 30.

items.title: One decision, not twelve
items.body: At 6 pm, tired, you don't want to choose between twelve cards. You open the app and there's one block, with the reason underneath.

items.title: Three questions, with the right page
items.body: Miss one and the app shows the answer and where it comes from in your materials. Then it asks again.

items.when: On a day that didn't happen
items.title: Nothing bad happens
items.body: A class dinner, the flu, just tired. The next day the plan quietly reshuffles and tells you what changed. You can undo it.

items.title: The time you have, well used
items.body: Not enough for a block, enough for your due reviews. Six cards, including the one you missed yesterday.

items.title: One decision per screen
items.body: Every screen has one obvious main action. Everything else is a tap away, not in your face.

items.title: No punishment
items.body: Missing a day is normal. No red overdue counters, no streaks lost to the flu.

items.title: Honesty over comfort
items.body: If the material won't fit before the test, the app says so and suggests what to cut. Uni tells you when something isn't in your materials.

items.title: Your data is yours
items.body: Works without an account and offline. The minimum leaves your phone, and you know what and where.

uni.title: A tutor that knows
uni.body: Uni is Unipedia's tutor. Unlike any old chatbot, it knows your semester: your courses, your exam dates and the materials you've added.
bullets: Explains topics from your PDFs, slides and photos.
Builds a plan up to your next test in one conversation.
Says «this isn't in your materials» when that's the case.

privacy.title: Your notebook
privacy.body: You can use Unipedia without an account: everything stays on your device. If you want to sync between phone and computer, you create an account, and you decide.

items.title: No account
items.body: Local mode on your device, from minute one.

items.title: Offline
items.body: Plan, focus and cards work without a connection.

items.title: You know what leaves
items.body: AI is only used when you turn Uni on, and you're told where the data goes.

items.a: For secondary school and university students, studying in English, Portuguese or Spanish.
No. You can use everything on your device. An account lets you back up and sync your notebook across devices.

items.q: Does it work on phone and computer?
items.a: Yes. It opens in the browser on either one and adapts to the screen.

items.q: Where do the practice questions come from?
items.a: From the materials you add (PDFs, slides, past papers) and your notes. You can also write cards by hand.

items.q: What if I miss a day?
items.a: That's fine. The plan redistributes what was left, tells you what changed and you can undo it.
Yes, Uni uses Google AI (Gemini) and only works once you turn it on. The rest of the app doesn't need it.

faq.q: Do I need an account to get started?
faq.a: No. You can use everything on your device. An account only lets you back up and sync across devices.

faq.q: What happens to the photo of my timetable?
faq.a: It's sent to Uni (Google's Gemini) only to read your courses, classes and dates. You can turn automatic reading off in Settings and type it in yourself.

faq.q: What if my timetable changes mid-semester?
faq.a: Import it again or edit the course. The plan recalculates and shows «Undo».

meta.title: Study plan — Unipedia
meta.description: A weekly plan that knows your tests, fits back in what slipped and adjusts when life happens. Always with «Undo».

plano.title: Your week sorts
plano.sub: With your courses and tests in the app, the plan spreads the material across the days you picked, starts the heaviest topics early and rearranges everything when a day doesn't go to plan.

sections.title: Built around your tests
sections.body: You choose the days and hours per day; the plan does the rest. Each day shows the time, course, topic and minutes of every block.
points: Day and week views
Your own rhythm, for example Monday to Saturday, 2 h a day
«Update» rebuilds the plan whenever you like

sections.title: What slipped fits back in
sections.body: A block you didn't do shows up under «Left behind». You choose: fit it in another day, move it to today or discard it.
points: No overdue counters, no punishment
The new plan already counts what was left undone
«Plan updated · Undo» whenever it changes

sections.title: Today shows only what matters now
sections.body: The Today screen shows the day's focus. If you only have a little time, «I have 10, 25 or 50 min» gives you the block that fits.
points: Mark blocks as done with one tap
Notes and tasks on the same screen
Today's agenda and upcoming tests

sections.title: Focus with a shield, when you want it
sections.body: Each block opens a timer with an optional distraction shield and ambient sound. If you finish early, your real minutes are kept and the rest goes back into the plan.
points: Full screen and keep screen on
Silence, rain or white noise
At the end, practice on the block's topic

items.title: Add courses and tests

items.title: Pick your rhythm
items.body: Days and hours per day, in Automatic or Manual.

items.title: Open Today
items.body: And start with the first block.

faq.q: What if I don't know my test dates yet?
faq.a: The plan starts with balanced study across your courses and reorganises itself once you add the dates.

faq.q: Can I move blocks by hand?
faq.a: Yes. In manual mode your blocks stay as you left them; in automatic mode every change shows «Plan updated · Undo».

faq.q: What happens if I miss a day?
faq.a: That day's blocks appear under «Left behind». You fit them in, move them to today or discard them; nothing counts against you.

faq.q: Does the app keep copies of my Drive files?
faq.a: It keeps a reference to each file and reads the content when you need it, with your Google Drive permission. Files from your device stay in the browser's local storage.

faq.q: Can I use my course's shared Drive?
faq.a: Yes. Paste the link to the shared folder and it becomes part of your library.

faq.q: Do I need to organise my folders in a particular way?
faq.a: It helps to have one folder per course, named after it. The folder guide on the page itself explains how.

meta.title: The Unis — Unipedia
meta.description: One Uni per course: pick its shape, colour and personality, and it grows from Egg to Master with your real mastery. Plus a tutor that reads your materials and creates notebooks, quizzes and podcasts.

uni.title: A study buddy
uni.sub: Uni is the face of Unipedia: a study companion you adopt for each course and that grows with you. It's also the tutor that knows your semester and answers from your own materials.

sections.title: Adopt a Uni for each course
sections.body: Choose its shape (Cloud, Drop, Star, Crystal or Leaf), colour, name, teaching personality and even the language it uses with you in that course.
points: Personalities like Curious or Coach
Examples first, theory or exercises
A voice for each Uni, if you like

sections.title: It grows with your real mastery
sections.body: Each Uni goes from Egg to Apprentice, Explorer, Specialist and Master, only through real mastery of the course: reviews, practice and tests. It can't be bought or faked.
points: Mastery from 0 to 100 per course
Next stage and next test in view
When it's done, it teaches its method to the next Uni

sections.title: The shelf, the pets and a little love
sections.body: Your Unis live on the Shelf, with diplomas for the courses you mastered. You earn colours and micropets as you study, and there's daily energy to fill with sessions and tasks.
points: Unis & Diplomas
Looks & Micropets
A pat for your Uni counts too

sections.title: And a real tutor
sections.body: In the Tutor, Uni explains topics from your materials, quizzes you, builds plans up to your next test and suggests sessions or cards that are only saved if you confirm. Uni's Notebook turns notes, PDFs and recordings into study guides, quizzes with citations, summaries and podcasts.
points: Photos and PDFs in the chat
Voice notes transcribed and PDF export
Up to 15 messages a day included
